title: Advanced PL/pgSQL Functions
description: Execute dynamic queries with EXECUTE, work with RECORD variables, and return structured output.

data.text: When query structures must vary dynamically at runtime (e.g. dynamic sorting or table names), PL/pgSQL provides **`EXECUTE`** with parameter binding (`USING`).

data.title: Safe Dynamic SQL Execution with EXECUTE ... USING
data.content: Safely injecting table names and parameter bindings to prevent SQL injection.

data.text: Returning Structured Data from Dynamic SQL

`EXECUTE ... INTO` assigns a single row to a variable or record, while `RETURN QUERY EXECUTE` streams a full result set. Both support the `USING` clause, which binds parameters safely. Identifiers, which cannot be parameterized, must be quoted with `format('%I', ...)`.

data.title: Search any table by column, safely
data.content: The table and column names are validated as identifiers with `%I`; the search value is passed as a bound parameter with `%L` through USING.

data.title: Dynamic SQL is the injection surface
data.text: Any user-influenced string concatenated into `EXECUTE` is a SQL injection risk. The rule is simple: quote identifiers with `%I`, pass values through the `USING` clause, and never build a value into the string. If a table name has to come from user input, validate it against an allowlist of known tables before calling `format`.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always use `format('%I', identifier)` to escape table and column names in dynamic SQL.
Always use `USING param` to parameterize values passed to `EXECUTE`.
Use `INTO variable` to store single scalar query results.
